details: Multi-agent LLM systems are hard to co-optimize as a whole: full-parameter training is costly and text-mediated agent interaction adds latency and sequential dependency.
Recursive/looped language models scale reasoning depth inside one model; the paper asks whether agent collaboration itself can be scaled by recursion.

RecursiveMAS: casts an entire heterogeneous multi-agent system as a single latent-space recursive computation, treating each agent as a 'layer' of a looped model whose latent thoughts are passed agent-to-agent and fed back from the last agent to the first, with only the final agent decoding text.

RecursiveLink: a lightweight two-layer residual projection module used (i) inside each agent to map last-layer hidden states back into its input embedding space for latent auto-regressive generation, and (ii) across agents to map between different hidden dimensions.

Inner–outer loop training: agents are frozen and only RecursiveLink is trained — inner loop aligns each agent's latent thoughts to its input-embedding semantics (cosine regression to ground-truth embeddings), outer loop backpropagates cross-entropy on the final answer through the unrolled recursion for shared credit assignment.
Sequential (Planner → Critic → Solver, chain-of-agents).
Mixture (Math/Code/Science specialists in parallel + Summarizer).
Distillation (large Expert + small fast Learner).
Deliberation (Reflector + Tool-Caller with Python interpreter and Tavily search API).
Heterogeneous off-the-shelf agents from Qwen/Qwen3(.5), Llama-3, Gemma3, Mistral; a 'light' version with sub-1.5B agents and a 'scaled' version with 5–10B agents.

Training set curated from s1K (math), m1K (medical/science), OpenCodeReasoning (code), ARPO-SFT (tool use); role-specific supervision targets synthesized per collaboration pattern (e.g., Qwen3.5-397B-A17B rewrites answers into planner/critic targets).
Benchmarks: MATH500, AIME2025/2026 (Pass@10), GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, LiveCodeBench-v6, MBPP Plus, HotpotQA, Bamboogle.
All LLM parameters frozen; only inner/outer RecursiveLink trained with AdamW, lr 5e-4, cosine schedule, batch size 4, max seq 4096.
Recursion depth r ∈ {1,2,3} at both training and inference (matched at inference to training rounds by default); latent thought length m ablated.
Inference: top-p 0.95, temperature 0.6 (0.2 for code), task-dependent max length up to 16k for AIME; mean over five runs; H100/A100 GPUs; HuggingFace + vLLM.
Single agents from each pattern, off-the-shelf plus LoRA and full SFT on the same data.
Recursion-based: LoopLM (Ouro-2.6B), single recursive LM, and Recursive-TextMAS (identical structure but text-mediated interaction).
Multi-agent frameworks: TextGrad (textual-gradient optimization) and Mixture-of-Agents; matched backbones, trainable-parameter counts, recursion depth, and training data.
Proposition: per-agent runtime with N agents, context t, generation m, hidden d_h, vocab |V| — RecursiveMAS Θ(N(m d_h² + (t+m)d_h² + (t+m)²d_h)) vs text-based Θ(N(m|V|d_h + ...)).
Theorem (gradient stability) under assumptions that text-based recursion equals W_in softmax(W_out h) with O(1) spectral norms, Kaiming-initialized W1,W2, W3 = I, and token entropy ≤ ε.

key_findings.finding: Recursive latent collaboration across agents improves accuracy over strong single-agent, multi-agent, and recursive baselines while being cheaper at inference.
key_findings.evidence: Average accuracy gain of 8.3% over the strongest baseline per benchmark across nine benchmarks, with 1.2x–2.4x end-to-end inference speedup and 34.6%–75.6% token reduction; gains over TextGrad/LoopLM reach 18.1% on AIME2025, 13.0% on AIME2026, and 5.4% on GPQA-Diamond.

key_findings.finding: The advantage over text-mediated recursion grows with recursion depth, in both accuracy and efficiency.
key_findings.evidence: Versus Recursive-TextMAS, average accuracy improvement of 8.1% at r=1, 19.6% at r=2, 20.2% at r=3; speedup grows 1.2x → 1.9x → 2.4x and token reduction 34.6% → 75.6% across r=1,2,3.

key_findings.finding: Training-time and inference-time recursion depths scale complementarily.
key_findings.evidence: Performance landscape over training × inference recursion rounds shows deeper inference improves systems trained with fewer rounds, while deeper training shifts the whole frontier upward, with best results in the high-high regime; PCA of generated vs ground-truth answer embeddings over 500 QA pairs shows progressive alignment from r=1 to r=3, and case studies show wrong answers at r=1 corrected at r=2/3.

key_findings.finding: Theory justifies latent over text mediation: lower runtime complexity and non-vanishing gradients through recursion.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition replaces per-step vocabulary decoding cost m|V|d_h with latent transform m d_h² (d_h ≪ |V|); Theorem shows text-based recursive links have Jacobian norm ≤ O(ε) for confident (low-entropy) tokens while RecursiveLink's residual Jacobian norm is ≥ Ω(1 − sqrt(log(1/δ)/d_h)) with probability ≥ 1−δ.

key_findings.finding: The design is cheap and largely insensitive to structure, with the residual two-layer link and a modest latent budget being the key choices.
key_findings.evidence: Res+2-layer link beats 1-layer / 2-layer / Res+1-layer variants (e.g., 88.0 vs 85.6/84.4/86.7 on MATH500; 66.2 on GPQA-D); training uses 13.12M trainable params (0.31%), 15.29GB peak memory, $4.27 cost vs LoRA ($6.64, 66.9% avg) and full SFT ($9.67, 68.6%) while reaching 74.9% average accuracy; performance saturates around latent length m≈80; gains generalize to Mixture (+6.2% over best specialist), Deliberation (+4.8%), Distillation (+8.0% over learner with 1.5x speed over expert).
